name: Ngen

catalog_locator: sec. 8 'Tone', p.113 (Table 5, Table 6 pp.113-114); sec. 5 'Feet', pp.110-111
catalog_quote: Ngen has 3 level tones, shown in Table 5. Stress has not been observed. ... It is assumed in this paper that the basic tone-bearing unit (TBU) is a single vowel (including ŋ) or 'minor syllable', but a 'major' one, because sequences of two vowels CVV in major syllables can bear either similar or dissimilar tones e.g.: sùà 'money', tāá 'pothole', gíè 'good'. Melodies at the word level are diverse. A few observations can be shown here. Tone melodies on disyllabic feet exhibit all possible combinations except LH, as shown in Table 6.

Российская лингвистическая экспедиция в Кот-д'Ивуар и орфографические реформы в южных языках манде [Russian linguistic field trips to Côte d'Ivoire and orthography reforms in the South Mande languages]. Кунсткамера (Kunstkamera) 2019, № 4(6): 107-121. doi:10.31250/2618-8619-2019-4(6)-107-121
tone_statements.quote: Все эти языки политонические: половина из них (уан, муан, гуро, нген, бен) имеет по 3 уровневых тона (трехтоновый также и язык мано, распространенный в Гвинее и Либерии), половина (западный дан, кла-дан, гоо, тура, яурэ, гбан) — по 4; восточный дан имеет 5 уровневых тонов, при этом гуро, бен, западный и восточный дан, гбан имеют также модулированные тоны. Во всех этих языках тоны несут большую функциональную нагрузку и служат не только для лексического контраста, но и для выражения многочисленных грамматических значений.
tone_statements.translation: All these languages are polytonic: half of them (Wan, Mwan, Guro, Ngen, Beng) have 3 level tones each (Mano, spoken in Guinea and Liberia, is also three-tone), half (Western Dan, Kla-Dan, Goo, Tura, Yaure, Gban) have 4 each; Eastern Dan has 5 level tones, and Guro, Beng, Western and Eastern Dan and Gban also have modulated (contour) tones. In all these languages tones carry a heavy functional load and serve not only for lexical contrast but also for the expression of numerous grammatical meanings.

audit.reasoning: The record rests on the only published phonology of Ngen (Korol 2021, publisher PDF held), and the deciding quotation 'Ngen has 3 level tones.. Stress has not been observed' is verbatim at p.113 with Tables 5-6 on pp.113-114 as cited. Glottolog lists no grammar or other phonology; web search of the author's profiles and Mande venues finds nothing later on Ngen prosody. Korol 2022 (Mandenkan 68, downloaded now, open access) uses H/M/L plus a falling tone and grammatical low/high-tone verb forms, confirming the tonal coding and saying nothing about stress. Identity is clean (ISO gnj, Djonkro(u), Prikro prefecture in both papers). Only unpublished HSE theses and a forthcoming PhD grammar could add detail; neither is likely to change 'tonal, no word stress'.

sources.note: Introduction classifies all South Mande languages as tonal and puts Ngen in the group with 3 level tones (with Wan, Mwan, Guro, Beng), versus 4-level (W. Dan, Kla-Dan, Goo, Tura, Yaure, Gban) and 5-level (E. Dan); Ngen is not among the languages listed as also having contour ('modulated') tones; tones carry heavy lexical and grammatical load in all of them. Independent confirmation (by the expedition leader) of Korol 2021's 3-level analysis.
